_comment: The AUTHORED half of the comparison section: names, families, prose, and
which columns the table shows. Every actual number is left null and filled
by demo/build_demo.py from the JSON that the measuring scripts write:
python kevin_pipeline/fair_comparison.py --json-out outputs/measured/fair_comparison.json
python evaluate.py --class-conf-threshold 0.97 \
--checkpoint outputs/pointnet2_checkpoints/epoch39_multitask_model.pt \
--json-out outputs/measured/evaluate_pointnet2.json
python demo/build_demo.py --only metrics
The split exists so that a number on the page can never be something a
human typed. Prose is written; numbers are measured. If the measured files
are absent the exporter skips and the previously generated payloads/
metrics.js is kept, so a fresh clone still renders.
The MSE values come from fair_comparison.py, which puts all three
candidates on ONE shared scale. Do not substitute the per-run
train_metrics.json numbers: PointNet++'s recon loss there is a Chamfer
distance in metres while SalsaNext's and Kevin's are normalized MSE. Those
differ by roughly three orders of magnitude and are not comparable.

models.name: PointNet++
models.notes: Consumes 32,768 raw xyz points and emits 2,048 free-form points. Its reconstruction is reprojected onto the real ray grid before scoring, so this MSE survives an extra approximation step the other two don't need — the gap is, if anything, understated.

models.name: CNN autoencoder
models.notes: Reconstruction only — it was never built with a classification head, so it is excluded from the accuracy comparison rather than given an invented number.

models.name: SalsaNext
models.notes: Outputs on the native (64,1024) grid, so no reprojection is needed. An early version scored 0.0118 MSE until an AdaptiveAvgPool2d before the latent projection was found to be discarding the positional information only the reconstruction decoder needed — fixing that improved reconstruction 9.2x.

_comment: No bar on SSIM deliberately: all three land in 0.952-0.972, so a
zero-based bar reads as three identical full bars, and a zoomed axis
would dramatise a difference that is genuinely small. The number alone
is the honest presentation; MSE is where the real spread is.

perClass._comment: model + threshold are authored; macroF1 and rows come from evaluate.py --json-out.
